author: product-requirements-expert
title: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected
summary: A booked visit can be corrected afterwards: the correction starts from the visit's recorded date and description, is held to the same rules as the original booking, and amends the existing visit rather than leaving a second one behind. Cancelling a visit stays out of scope (NG-10).
acceptance_criteria: Opening the correction for a booked visit shows the same form the booking used, carrying that visit's current date and description.
Submitting a correction with a description and a date later than today updates that visit to the corrected date and description, and the owner's record is shown.
Submitting a correction with a blank description, or a date of today or earlier, refuses the correction, names the offending field, and shows the form again.
Correcting the single visit of a pet leaves that pet with exactly one visit — the correction updates in place and creates no additional visit record.
Edge case 3: a visit whose date has already passed cannot be corrected without also moving its date into the future, because the future-date rule applies to every submission.
non_goals: Cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-10)
Moving a visit to a different pet or owner
Any record of who corrected a visit, or when — no lifecycle or audit state
notes: NG-5 was narrowed by product-owner decision 2026-08-07 and retired to the PRD's Superseded list; NG-10 succeeds it and declines cancellation alone. Path recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-07-non-goal-visit-correction.md. Open for the design stage, deliberately not a requirement: the product owner specified no navigation to the correction from the owner's record, so reachability is unresolved — raise it if the design needs it. docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for the new ADR; that file is outside this agent's write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correction is the existing child-record-edit pattern applied to Visit. PetController already demonstrates it for Pet under the same aggregate: an init/process route pair under /owners/{ownerId}, bean validation plus a controller-level cross-field rule, redisplay of the same createOrUpdate template on failure, redirect to the owner detail page on success, and the write going through OwnerRepository as the sole path into the owner-pet-visit graph (system-design.md Overview, Contracts, and ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization). The one adjustment is the shared @ModelAttribute seeding method in VisitController: today it unconditionally builds a new Visit and attaches it to the pet, which is exactly what an edit route must not do. Mirror PetController.findPet and branch on an optional visitId path variable. No new package, no new type outside the owner package, no dependency change, no docs/system-design.md edit — the Contracts row for VisitController describes current state and doc-sync updates it after the code lands. Basis: direct reads of VisitController.java, PetController.java, Owner.java, Pet.java, and the template (no IDE oracle connected in this dispatch, so the claim rests on reads rather than symbol resolution).
integration_points: VisitController gains GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit alongside the existing /visits/new pair; both pairs share loadPetWithVisit, minVisitDate, and the pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm view
Pet gains a getVisit(Integer id) lookup mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id) (Owner.java:117-127), so the correction target is reached by traversing owner -> pet -> visit
The write stays OwnerRepository.save(owner) on the loaded aggregate; cascade from Owner issues an UPDATE against the existing visit row, no INSERT
No template change is required: the form posts to the current URL with no action attribute, so pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm serves both routes unchanged

patterns.description: child-record edit pair under the owner aggregate: initUpdateForm returns the shared form, processUpdateForm validates, redisplays on error, saves through OwnerRepository, and redirects to redirect:/owners/{ownerId} with a flash message. Name the new methods initUpdateVisitForm / processUpdateVisitForm to match.

the optional-path-variable branch in a @ModelAttribute seeding method (@PathVariable(name = "petId", required = false) Integer petId; new Pet() when null, the loaded one otherwise). This is the shape loadPetWithVisit must take for visitId.
loadPetWithVisit runs before every mapping in the controller and today always calls pet.addVisit(new Visit()). The edit branch must return the visit already in pet.getVisits() and attach nothing.
identity lookup over a cascaded child collection, returning null when absent — the shape for Pet.getVisit(Integer).

risks.risk: The pet gains a second visit. loadPetWithVisit is a @ModelAttribute method, so it runs before the edit GET and the edit POST as well as the create routes; its unconditional pet.addVisit(new Visit()) would attach a transient visit to the eagerly-fetched, cascade-ALL collection, and OwnerRepository.save would INSERT it. This is the acceptance criterion most likely to be missed.
risks.mitigation: Branch on @PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId: null keeps today's behaviour exactly; non-null returns pet.getVisit(visitId) and calls no add. Because the returned instance is the form-backing object, Spring binds the submitted date and description straight onto the visit already inside the loaded owner graph — prefill and in-place update both fall out, and there is no code path that can create a Visit on the edit route. Cover it with theCorrectedPetShouldNotGainAnAdditionalVisit asserting pet.getVisits() has size 1 on the same Owner instance the @MockitoBean repository hands the controller (VisitControllerTests.init already holds it), not with a Mockito verify.

risks.risk: Copying PetController.updatePetDetails into VisitController. That helper exists only because PetController loads the owner twice — findOwner and findPet each call owners.findById, producing two detached graphs, so the bound pet is a different object from the one that gets saved. VisitController has no such split: loadPetWithVisit loads once and puts that owner, that pet, and the visit into the model together.
risks.mitigation: Do not add a copy step and do not add a second @ModelAttribute("owner") method that reloads the owner. A reload would silently save an unmutated graph — the correction would appear to succeed and change nothing. Resolve the owner parameter of the POST from the model, as processNewVisitForm already does.

risks.risk: Identifier tampering: visitId arrives from the URL and could name a visit belonging to another owner's pet (threat model, mass-assignment / identifier-tampering row).
risks.mitigation: Resolve the visit only by traversing owner -> pet -> visit; never add a global visit lookup or a VisitRepository. An unknown visitId throws IllegalArgumentException in loadPetWithVisit, matching the existing pet-not-found branch. Keep the @InitBinder disallowing id and *.id so the identity can never come from the form.

risks.risk: Breaking the i18n bundle-parity test. A new message key added to messages.properties alone fails I18nPropertiesSyncTest.checkI18nPropertyFilesAreInSync across the eleven bundles, and new literal text in a template fails checkNonInternationalizedStrings.
risks.mitigation: Introduce no new message key and no new template text. The submit button keeps the addVisit label and the success flash message stays a controller-side literal, consistent with the create flow's "Your visit has been booked". If a label change proves genuinely necessary, the key must land in all eleven bundles in the same change.

notes: Reachability is out of this slice, deliberately. The four acceptance criteria are complete HTTP contracts and MockMvc drives the routes directly, so no UI affordance is needed for the slice to be testable or coherent as specified. Adding an "Edit Visit" link would change owners/ownerDetails.html — a REQ-OWN-003 surface, not a REQ-VIS-003 one — and would need a new message key in all eleven bundles. It is requirement-shaped work: raise it with the product owner as its own slice if the correction should be reachable from the owner's record. The route ships unreachable from the UI until then; that is a known, recorded gap rather than an oversight. docs/adr/README.md now carries the index row for 2026-08-07-non-goal-visit-correction.md, appended in date order and matching the table's Date / Decision / Status shape. Vocabulary: ubiquitous-language.md defines Visit and forbids Appointment, Booking, Consultation, and Treatment; it names no term for the act of amending one, so the PRD's "correction" in prose and the /edit route segment (matching the pet edit route and the createOrUpdateVisitForm template name) do not conflict — no new term is being coined here. Optional Refactor-step cleanups, neither required: extract the repeated "pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm" into a private view-name constant as PetController does, and extract the shared future-date check now used by both POST methods. No design-doc-autofix records to audit.

rationale: risk triggers present (multi-module, oversize, design-revision); full battery

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: loadPetWithVisit's branch on the nullable visitId is clearly documented: the Javadoc explains not just what each branch does but why (new-and-attach for booking vs. return-unattached for correction, so binding writes onto the existing graph member), which is exactly the non-obvious behavior a cold reader needs

VisitController correctly avoids the PetController.updatePetDetails copy-field pattern the design warned against — because the @ModelAttribute method loads the visit once and binds directly onto the graph member, processUpdateVisitForm needs no second lookup or field-by-field copy; the asymmetry with PetController is well-explained by the inline comment above processUpdateVisitForm ('do not reload the owner here, or the correction would be discarded')

Pet.getVisit(Integer) mirrors Owner.getPet(Integer) faithfully: same Javadoc phrasing, same isNew()/Objects.equals guard, same linear-scan-return-null shape, verified by direct comparison against Owner.java:117-127

The VIEWS_VISIT_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FORM constant and rejectDateNotInTheFuture extraction remove real duplication (four literal call sites, two copies of the date-rejection check) without changing behavior
The unknown-visitId IllegalArgumentException mirrors the existing pet-not-found branch's message shape (childId not found for parentId)
./gradlew checkFormat passes

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Identifier tampering: the visit is resolved only by traversal (owners.findById(ownerId) -> owner.getPet(petId) -> pet.getVisit(visitId)). No VisitRepository, no global lookup. Owner.getPet and the new Pet.getVisit both iterate only the parent's own collection and use Objects.equals, so a mismatched triple (visit of another pet, pet of another owner) resolves to null and throws before any write. The POST handler saves the same traversed owner aggregate, so there is no second, unguarded path to the row.

Mass assignment on the persistent form-backing Visit: the controller-wide @InitBinder (VisitController:53-56) sets setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id"), matching OwnerController and PetController. Visit exposes only date and description beyond the blocked id, so a crafted POST cannot re-target the bound instance at another visit's identity. Owner-side over-binding via @ModelAttribute Owner plus owners.save(owner) is identical in kind and reach to the pre-existing processNewVisitForm create path; this slice adds no field, no entity, and no cascade the create flow did not already expose.

Unknown visitId throws IllegalArgumentException carrying only the two integer path variables. visitId binds as Integer, so non-numeric input fails conversion before the message is built; no reflected string reaches the response. No server.error.include-message override is set, so Spring Boot's default (never) keeps the message out of the error page. Nothing beyond an existence signal is disclosed, and that signal is already inherent to the unauthenticated read surface the project accepts under NG-1.

Output escaping: pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html is unchanged and renders every user-derived value through th:text (visit description, pet name, owner name). Swept src/main/resources/templates for th:utext and inline unescaped output; none in the visit path.

No new state-changing surface class beyond the existing create POST: same aggregate, same repository call, same validation (@NotBlank description plus the shared rejectDateNotInTheFuture future-date guard applied on every submission, so a past-dated visit cannot be saved by resubmission). Absence of authentication, authorization, and CSRF tokens is recorded project scope (NG-1, docs/system-design.md#security-context), not a defect introduced here.

Supply chain: the change set touches no build.gradle, pom.xml, or version catalog, and adds no dependency or plugin. No secrets introduced; swept the diff's added lines for token/password/secret/key/credential/Authorization/Bearer with no hits.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The load-bearing no-additional-visit proof (`theCorrectedPetShouldNotGainAnAdditionalVisit`, `hasSize(1)` on `this.owner`) and `verify(this.owners).save(this.owner)` only inspect the in-memory object graph handed back by a fully-mocked `OwnerRepository`; no test in this file (new or pre-existing) ever exercises a real `OwnerRepository`/Hibernate save. The design record (line 8) named the exact hazard this test is meant to rule out: a transient `Visit` attached to the eagerly-fetched, cascade-ALL `visits` collection getting INSERTed by `OwnerRepository.save(owner)`, calling it 'the acceptance criterion most likely to be missed.' A regression that made `processUpdateVisitForm`/`loadPetWithVisit` call `pet.addVisit(...)` on a *copy* or that otherwise mutated the graph after the mocked `save` was invoked would still leave `owner.getPet(...).getVisits()` at size 1 in this test, while a real cascade-ALL save could still insert a duplicate row — the mock cannot distinguish 'no second visit was ever created' from 'the second visit was created after or independent of the point this assertion reads.' No integration test anywhere in the repository (`PetClinicIntegrationTests`, `MySqlIntegrationTests`, `PostgresIntegrationTests` all have zero visit references) exercises visit persistence at all, for creation or correction. This may be an accepted scope decision consistent with the rest of the `VisitController` suite (which also never hits real persistence), but given the design itself flagged this specific hazard as the one most likely to slip through, a human call on whether a real-repository test belongs in this slice or a follow-up is warranted.

Pet.getVisit(Integer)'s null/absent branch, and the corresponding `visit == null` -> IllegalArgumentException branch in VisitController.loadPetWithVisit, are completely untested. Confirmed via JaCoCo branch coverage: Pet.getVisit shows 3/6 branches missed, VisitController.loadPetWithVisit shows 2/6 missed — the only branch exercised is the happy path where visitId resolves to an existing visit on the pet. This is exactly the mitigation the design record (line 8) names for its identifier-tampering risk ('An unknown visitId throws IllegalArgumentException ... resolve the visit only by traversing owner -> pet -> visit'), yet nothing regresses it: a change that silently swallowed an unresolved visitId, or resolved a visitId belonging to a different pet, would pass the full suite today.
findings.fix: Add a test posting or getting /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit with a visitId that does not exist on the pet (e.g. TEST_VISIT_ID + 1) and assert the request fails (5xx or the same behavior the existing pet-not-found path produces) rather than silently proceeding; this exercises both the controller branch and Pet.getVisit's null return.

findings.description: The corrected-visit description "Rash cleared, follow-up check" is a bare literal retyped in four places across three tests rather than declared once as a named constant, violating testing-principles.md's Three-Tier Data Naming (Tier 3 elimination) and Derived Expectations sections. In theVisitCorrectionShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlaceAndShowTheOwnerRecord specifically, the assertion at line 154 (`assertThat(corrected.getDescription()).isEqualTo("Rash cleared, follow-up check")`) re-types the same string submitted at line 147 instead of comparing against the value that was actually sent — a copy-paste slip between the two literals would go undetected. `LocalDate.now().plusDays(10)` is likewise repeated as a bare expression at lines 141, 162, and 174 instead of a shared constant.
findings.fix: Introduce class-level constants (e.g. CORRECTED_VISIT_DESCRIPTION, CORRECTED_VISIT_DATE) alongside the existing BOOKED_VISIT_DATE/BOOKED_VISIT_DESCRIPTION, use them as the submitted param in every test that needs a valid corrected value, and assert against the same constant in theVisitCorrectionShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlaceAndShowTheOwnerRecord instead of a re-typed literal.

findings.description: PRD edge case 3 for REQ-VIS-003 ('A visit whose date has already passed cannot be corrected without also moving its date into the future, because the future-date rule applies to every submission and not only to the first') has no test that traces to it. theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheDateIsNotInTheFuture covers the general non-future-date rule for a correction submission, but the fixture visit (BOOKED_VISIT_DATE) is always future-dated, so nothing in the test demonstrates the scenario the edge case actually names: a visit whose *stored* date has already lapsed. testing-principles.md's Edge Case Coverage checklist expects edge-case numbers to be traceable to prd.md's numbering.
findings.fix: Either rename/comment the existing test to note it covers REQ-VIS-003 edge case 3, or add a dedicated test with a lapsed-date fixture visit whose correction is submitted with an unchanged past date and assert refusal, naming the PRD edge case in a short comment.

approved_aspects: initUpdateVisitForm/processUpdateVisitForm follow the PetController child-record-edit pattern the design specified: same-template redisplay on error, redirect to owner detail on success, no second owner reload

theVisitCorrectionFormShouldBePrefilledWithTheVisitBeingCorrected and the blank-description/non-future-date refusal tests genuinely exercise their named behavior — verified by reading processUpdateVisitForm's call to rejectDateNotInTheFuture and Visit's @NotBlank, not incidental passes

All 9 tests in VisitControllerTests pass under ./gradlew test; no JUnit assertEquals/assertTrue, fluent AssertJ and MockMvc/Hamcrest matchers used consistently with the existing OwnerControllerTests convention
Four-phase structure observed with blank-line separation and no phase-comment narration

No new package, no new type outside the owner package, no dependency change. The Contracts table is now corrected in the same slice as the code it describes (see notes).

Pet gains a getVisit(Integer id) lookup mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id), so the correction target is reached by traversing owner -> pet -> visit
The write stays OwnerRepository.save(owner) on the loaded aggregate; cascade from Owner issues an UPDATE against the existing visit row, no INSERT

patterns.description: child-record edit pair under the owner aggregate: initUpdateForm returns the shared form, processUpdateForm validates, redisplays on error, saves through OwnerRepository, and redirects to redirect:/owners/{ownerId} with a flash message.
the optional-path-variable branch in a @ModelAttribute seeding method, the shape loadPetWithVisit takes for visitId.
identity lookup over a cascaded child collection, returning null when absent - the shape for Pet.getVisit(Integer).

risks.risk: The pet gains a second visit. loadPetWithVisit is a @ModelAttribute method, so it runs before the edit GET and the edit POST as well as the create routes; an unconditional pet.addVisit(new Visit()) would attach a transient visit to the eagerly-fetched, cascade-ALL collection and OwnerRepository.save would INSERT it.
risks.mitigation: Branch on @PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId: null keeps the booking behaviour exactly; non-null returns pet.getVisit(visitId) and calls no add. Cover it with a test asserting pet.getVisits() has size 1 on the same Owner instance the repository hands the controller, not with a Mockito verify. Implemented as specified and build-pass recorded.

risks.risk: Reloading the owner inside the edit POST would save an unmutated graph - the correction would appear to succeed and change nothing.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the owner parameter of the POST from the model, as processNewVisitForm already does; add no second @ModelAttribute("owner") method and no PetController-style copy step.

risks.risk: Identifier tampering: visitId arrives from the URL and could name a visit belonging to another owner's pet (threat model, mass-assignment / identifier-tampering row).
risks.mitigation: Resolve the visit only by traversing owner -> pet -> visit; never add a global visit lookup or a VisitRepository. An unknown visitId throws IllegalArgumentException in loadPetWithVisit, matching the existing pet-not-found branch. Keep the @InitBinder disallowing id and *.id so the identity can never come from the form.

risks.risk: Breaking the i18n bundle-parity test with a new message key or new literal template text.
risks.mitigation: Introduce no new message key and no new template text; the success flash stays a controller-side literal consistent with the create flow.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected
summary: A booked visit can be corrected afterwards: the correction starts from the visit's recorded date and description, is held to the same rules as the original booking, and amends the existing visit rather than leaving a second one behind. Cancelling a visit stays out of scope (NG-10).
acceptance_criteria: Opening the correction for a booked visit shows the same form the booking used, carrying that visit's current date and description.
Submitting a correction with a description and a date later than today updates that visit to the corrected date and description, and the owner's record is shown.
Submitting a correction with a blank description, or a date of today or earlier, refuses the correction, names the offending field, and shows the form again.
Correcting the single visit of a pet leaves that pet with exactly one visit — the correction updates in place and creates no additional visit record.
Edge case 3: a visit whose date has already passed cannot be corrected without also moving its date into the future, because the future-date rule applies to every submission.
non_goals: Cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-10)
Moving a visit to a different pet or owner
Any record of who corrected a visit, or when — no lifecycle or audit state
